**Don't follow the "Set up custom monitors" guide for these agent turns. Use a custom signal instead.**

**Why:** The custom monitors page says custom monitors are the previous approach to monitoring production traffic. For new implementations, it says to use **Signals** under Weave for Agents [S2]. Your instrumentation shows conversations and turns in the Agents view, so Signals is the matching workflow. The Monitors page's "choose operations" setup belongs to the older Calls workflow, so I wouldn't mix the two.

**What to do:** A custom signal scores agent turns against a behavior you define. It then shows the result as a tag in the Agents view [S3]. That fits a "needs human review" tag. The steps are [S1]:

1. In Forge, select your project. In the Weave project sidebar, click **Agents**, then the **Signals** tab.
2. Click **+ Create your first signal** or **New signal**, then choose **Custom Signal**.
3. In the **Custom tags** drawer, set:
   - **Tag name**: for example, a label for answers needing human review.
   - **Definition**: a prompt describing the behavior to detect. Weave sends it to an LLM judge. The judge scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches [S1]. Write your own criteria for when a human should review an answer. I didn't find review criteria in the docs.
   - **Scorer name**, and the **Inference model or custom runtime**. Serverless Inference is the default and uses credits from your CoreWeave Forge account [S1].
4. Optionally, expand **Advanced** to set:
   - **Include tool calls**.
   - **Only score turns matching** filters, such as agent, operation, tool, or model. If you leave this empty, every agent turn is scored, and multiple filters combine with `AND`.
   - **Sample rate**, which lowers cost for high-traffic agents.
5. Click **Create signal**. Weave then scores matching turns, and the tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab [S1].

**Caveats:**
- Check the built-in signals first, such as user frustration and jailbreaking. A custom signal is for behavior they don't cover [S3].
- The Signals UI only shows rows for spans that matched at least one tag. A tag signal can run successfully even if you don't see any output [S4].

**Limits of my search:** I only read the Signals custom-tag page and the monitors page. I didn't find a "human review" feature in them. I also didn't check whether alerts or review queues exist for this case.

[S4]: I did not read this passage directly. Treat the "no visible output" caveat as unverified until you check the View agent signals page.

For example, you can monitor your application's responses for correctness or helpfulness, or you can monitor user input to identify trends in what users ask your agents about. Monitors automatically store all scoring results in Weave's database, so you can analyze historical trends and patterns.

Monitors require no code changes to your application. Set them up using the Weights & Biases UI.

To score calls with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md).

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

## Signals and custom monitors

Use [signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/monitors.md), preset automated scorers for production traces, to get started with production monitoring quickly, then add custom monitors for evaluation criteria specific to your application.

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:

   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.

   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

# Set up custom monitors

> Passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues

> [!NOTE]
>
> Custom monitors are the previous approach to monitoring production traffic. For new implementations, use **Signals** under Weave for Agents. See [View agent signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

Monitors use LLM judges to passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues in your LLM applications. For example, you can monitor your application's responses for correctness or helpfulness, or you can monitor user input to identify trends in what users ask your agents about. Monitors automatically store all scoring results in Weave's database, so you can analyze historical trends and patterns.

You can monitor text, images, and audio in your application's input and output.

Monitors require no code changes to your application. Set them up using the Weights & Biases UI.

If you need to actively intervene in your application's behavior based on scores, use [guardrails](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/guardrails.md) instead.

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.
